purpose: S072 massive bulk electric polarization: common subtraction, exact tower, invariant thresholds and all-frequency classical pulse work

sources.reading_scope: Sections II.2, IV.2.1 and appendix A.1 read in full. Import the regulated vacuum 1+1-dimensional massive vector bubble, including the finite Ward contact and invariant pair threshold. No finite-temperature/density result, planar degeneracy or massive-only plasma dispersion is assigned to the sphere/LLL mixed model.

Section IV.2 threshold and invariant-momentum derivation, section IV.3 and appendix B read. The latter two were read in full; IV.3 was reread separately after a combined output truncated part of it. Reuse the distinction between local charge renormalization and finite magnetic response, and the pair-threshold singularity warning. No planar all-level numerical coefficient is transferred to the sphere.

Sphere spectrum equations 2.29-2.31 retained from the immediately preceding higher-Landau boundary audit, where they were reread. Exact sphere eigenvalues and total multiplicities only; no supersymmetric determinant or curved electric response is imported.

development_notes: The first checker run failed a 2e-14 Fourier normalization tolerance: 160-point double-precision Gauss-Legendre integration differed from the Bessel expression by 2.142730437526552e-14 at y=0.2. Independent 60-digit time integration found Gauss-Legendre error -1.8998357253340695e-14 and Bessel error 2.428947121924826e-15. The checker now uses the high-precision independent integral with a stricter 1e-14 tolerance; no formula, physical bound or pulse was changed.

Pulse work uses 300 massive levels, 512/1024/2048-node refinement and a separate analytic all-remaining-level tail bound. It does not use the general upper bound as a substitute for integrating the pulse.

The static subtraction is one common physical angular-mass cutoff subtraction. A finite magnetic response is retained and g_* is distinguished from the renormalized Maxwell g_R. Candidate values specify mu=1/b and g_R(mu)=k^-4 only as a comparison.

The exact all-frequency work result is a free vacuum linear-response theorem on R^(1,1) x S2 with a prescribed classical source. Its small value is relative to the pulse electric energy, not the negative opening energy.
The earlier S053 projected massless photon and determinant comparators are not identified with this massive electric sector; closed programs remain closed.
